entries.name: Python standard library
entries.purpose: Sole implementation language for SPS 2.0 core, governance and validators.
entries.observation_basis: Repository observation only. No external retrieval was performed for this entry, and none is claimed.

coverage_basis.current_version: Observed directly: validators execute under CPython 3.14.
coverage_basis.compatibility: Observed directly: the project enforces a stdlib-only policy and all tooling runs unmodified.
coverage_basis.recommended_practices: Observed directly: stdlib-only, no third-party imports, deterministic output.
coverage_basis.security_considerations: Observed directly: stdlib-only removes the third-party supply-chain surface, which is the basis of the dependency policy.
coverage_basis.mcp_tool_availability: Observed directly: not applicable; no MCP server is part of this choice.
coverage_basis.testing_approach: Observed directly: stdlib unittest plus repository negative suites.
coverage_basis.deployment_implications: Observed directly: no installation step; only an interpreter is required.

sources.observed: Every P5 module imports only the Python standard library and intra-repository modules.
Python is distributed under the PSF License; no third-party relicensing is claimed for SPS 2.0 code.

entries.notes: This entry is justified by direct repository observation rather than external retrieval. That is recorded explicitly so no reader mistakes observation for cited documentation.

entries.name: Core Web Vitals thresholds (LCP, INP, CLS)
entries.purpose: Threshold facts required by any SEO performance verifier.
entries.observation_basis: External retrieval from the official web.dev site on 2026-10-04.

coverage_basis.current_version: NOT OBSERVED. The vitals page states 'Last updated: 2024-10-31' and the methodology page 'Last updated: May 7, 2025', but no version number for the threshold set itself was exposed.
coverage_basis.security_considerations: NOT OBSERVED. No security section was retrieved for this set.
coverage_basis.recommended_practices: Observed: both pages direct readers to per-metric optimisation guides (Optimize LCP, Optimize INP, Optimize CLS).

observed_facts.metric_set: Core Web Vitals comprises LCP, CLS and INP. Observed on both pages.

verbatim_evidence.quote: we conclude that, while many origins meet the 0.05 threshold, the slightly less stringent CLS threshold of 0.1 strikes a better balance between quality of experience and achievability

For a 0.25 threshold, roughly 20% of phone origins, and 18% of desktop origins, would be classified as 'poor'. This falls in our target range of 10-30%, so we concluded that 0.25 is an acceptable 'poor' threshold.
we found that levels of shift from 0.15 and higher were consistently perceived as disruptive, while shifts of 0.1 and lower were noticeable but not excessively disruptive

sources.observed: Retrieved 2026-10-04, page last updated 2025-05-07. Contains the CLS derivation and thresholds; LCP and INP derivations were not present in the retrieved content.
Retrieved 2026-10-04, page last updated 2024-10-31. Confirms the Core Web Vitals set and Google's initiative ownership; the numeric table was again absent from the static content.

entries.notes: P2 recorded that the numeric tables were unreachable across three attempts. P6 re-attempted and CLS figures were obtained verbatim and agree with SRC-017, independently confirming that record. LCP and INP thresholds remain NOT OBSERVED after two further attempts. No LCP or INP figure is recorded anywhere in this repository. CONF-001 remains UNRESOLVED and this entry is therefore not selectable.
